name: Martin Luther King Jr.
life_summary: Martin Luther King Jr. was born Michael Luther King Jr. in Atlanta in 1929, the son of Baptist minister Martin Luther King Sr., who became pastor of Ebenezer Baptist Church in 1931. He was licensed to preach at Ebenezer in autumn 1947 and ordained there in February 1948, the year he graduated from Morehouse College. He then earned a Bachelor of Divinity at Crozer Theological Seminary (1951) and a PhD in systematic theology from Boston University (1955); the King Papers Project later found that his student papers and dissertation used sources without adequate attribution. He married Coretta Scott in 1953, and they had four children. As pastor of Dexter Avenue Baptist Church in Montgomery, Alabama (1954–1960), he led the 1955–1956 bus boycott as president of the Montgomery Improvement Association and in 1957 became the leader of what was soon named the Southern Christian Leadership Conference. From 1960 until his death he was co-pastor of Ebenezer with his father in Atlanta while taking part in campaigns in Albany, Birmingham, Selma, Chicago and elsewhere; in these years he was repeatedly jailed, spoke at the 1963 March on Washington, received the 1964 Nobel Peace Prize, publicly opposed the Vietnam War, and was monitored and wiretapped by the FBI. He was shot and killed in Memphis, Tennessee, on 4 April 1968 while supporting striking sanitation workers.

phases.label: Atlanta childhood
phases.summary: He grew up in the family home at 501 Auburn Avenue in Atlanta, son of the minister who became pastor of Ebenezer Baptist Church in 1931; his and his father's names changed to Martin Luther King around 1934. He attended local schools and entered Booker T. Washington High School in autumn 1942 after skipping ninth grade.

phases.label: Morehouse and Crozer years
phases.summary: He studied at Morehouse College in Atlanta from September 1944 to June 1948, was licensed to preach at Ebenezer in autumn 1947 and ordained and made assistant pastor there in February 1948. He then studied for a Bachelor of Divinity at Crozer Theological Seminary near Chester, Pennsylvania (September 1948 to May 1951).

phases.label: Boston University doctoral studies
phases.summary: He was a doctoral student in systematic theology at Boston University from September 1951, met Coretta Scott in Boston in early 1952 and married her in June 1953. During breaks he served as associate minister at Ebenezer in Atlanta until early 1954.

phases.label: Dexter Avenue pastorate
phases.summary: After a trial sermon in January 1954 he was called by Dexter Avenue Baptist Church in Montgomery on 7 March 1954 and began full-time on 1 September 1954; he received his PhD in June 1955. He led the 1955–1956 bus boycott as MIA president, led SCLC from 1957, and drafted his resignation in November 1959.

phases.label: Ebenezer co-pastorate, southern campaigns
phases.summary: From February 1960 he lived in Atlanta as co-pastor of Ebenezer with his father and as SCLC president. He joined or led campaigns in Albany (1961–1962), Birmingham (1963) and Selma (1965), spoke at the 1963 March on Washington and received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1964.
phases.place: Atlanta, Georgia (campaigns in Albany, Birmingham, Selma)

phases.label: Chicago, Vietnam, final campaigns
phases.summary: While still co-pastor at Ebenezer, he moved into a Chicago apartment in January 1966 for SCLC's housing campaign, opposed the Vietnam War in his April 1967 Riverside Church address and announced the Poor People's Campaign in December 1967. He was killed in Memphis in April 1968 while supporting striking sanitation workers.
phases.place: Atlanta, Georgia; Chicago, Illinois; Memphis, Tennessee

corrections: Dexter call date corrected: the church called King on 7 March 1954 (King Institute), not in April 1954; fixed in the Dexter phase summary and the 1 September 1954 event, and the installation (31 October 1954) is now cited to the King Institute installation-service entry.
Dexter phase: 'resigned in November 1959' reworded to 'drafted his resignation in November 1959', matching the Dexter encyclopedia (resignation dated 29 November 1959).
1960 co-pastor event: now states he accepted Ebenezer's call in November 1959 (Ebenezer encyclopedia) and moved on 1 February 1960; the unsupported 'near SCLC headquarters' clause was dropped.

Albany 1962 event: removed the claim that he was jailed until 10 August (the Albany Movement page gives 10 August as the day he agreed to leave Albany) and the claim that he drafted the 'final' sermons of Strength to Love there (that source says he finished the last sermons in early 1963); the event now says he worked on sermon drafts in jail that summer.

Birmingham event: removed 'for defying an injunction', which the cited page does not support, and the Chronology citation, which gives a different release date; release on 20 April is kept from the Birmingham Campaign page.
Home bombing event: removed 'he urged the crowd to remain calm', which no fetched page confirmed; added that the family was unharmed (Chronology).
SCLC event: 'president' changed to 'leader' (the Chronology says he was named chairman of the founding Southern Negro Leaders Conference).
Birth event: added the 501 Auburn Avenue address (Chronology, NPS) and replaced the New Georgia Encyclopedia citation with the NPS Birth Home page.
Morehouse graduation date of 8 June 1948 added from the Chronology.
Stabbing event: added the store name, Blumstein's (King Institute Curry entry).
Added an event for the 21–25 March 1965 Selma-to-Montgomery march to fill the 1964–1966 gap (Selma encyclopedia).

Removed the separate 4 April 1967 'Beyond Vietnam' event to stay within 25 events; the speech remains in the final phase and the life summary, and the criticism from newspapers and the NAACP was confirmed on the Beyond Vietnam page.
Final phase sources: replaced the Beyond Vietnam page with the Chronology, which also supports the December 1967 Poor People's Campaign announcement.
Assassination event: now says 'pronounced dead at St. Joseph's Hospital' and 'the day after his final speech at Mason Temple' (Memphis strike page), in place of the unconfirmed speech-title wording.

Life summary: FBI clause changed to 'monitored and wiretapped by the FBI' (FBI encyclopedia: monitoring from December 1955, wiretaps authorised in October 1963); added that King Sr became Ebenezer pastor in 1931; the plagiarism sentence was merged into the education sentence.
Childhood phase: the name change is now dated 'around 1934' because the King Sr encyclopedia describes a gradual change rather than a single dated event.
Note: the King Institute dissertation page says the degree was conferred in May 1955, while the Chronology and the Autobiography chapter give 5 June 1955; the event keeps 5 June 1955.
